config_schema.title: Config
config_schema.description:
Main configuration.

## This struct is the wrapper's half of the `--config` file

It owns `pipeline`, `source`, `sink`, `transforms`, `enrichment_tables` and
`dlq`.
scalo's own sections -- `metrics`, `logger`, `memory`, `scaling`,
`worker_pool`, `batch_processing`, `self_regulation`, `version_check`,
`otel_tracing` --
may sit beside them: scalo's cascade reads the same file as its settings
layer, and its env layer outranks the file. [`SCALO_CASCADE_SECTIONS`] lists
them, and [`warn_unreachable_scalo_settings`] warns for one in a
working-directory `config.yaml` read without `--config`, which scalo never
sees.

## Requires pod restart (bound at startup)

- `pipeline.name` — baked into Kafka `group_id`, metrics labels, tracing spans
- `source.*` — rdkafka consumer: connection, subscription, auth, TLS, buffers
- `sink.brokers` — rdkafka producer connection established at startup
- `sink.topic` — output topic (changing mid-stream risks data loss)
- `sink.compression` — rdkafka `compression.type` set at producer creation
- `sink.sasl.*` / `sink.tls.*` — security protocol set at producer creation
- `sink.max_buffer_bytes` — rdkafka `queue.buffering.max.kbytes` at creation
- `sink.librdkafka_options` — passed to `ClientConfig` at creation
- `transforms.*` — VRL programs compiled at startup, immutable for process lifetime
- `dlq.*` — the dead-letter queue is spawned at startup

## Accepted but not applied

[`Config::inert_settings`] is the list, and the wrapper warns at startup for
each one a deployment has actually set.

dlq.description:
Where a record the sink refuses for good goes: one over the sink's
size ceiling, or matched by an outbound `dlq` filter. scalo's type
verbatim. The default writes NDJSON files under `/var/spool/scalo/dlq`,
which the deployment contract declares writable. With `enabled: false`
such a record is dropped and counted on
`pipeline_dead_letters_dropped_total`.

name.description: Pipeline name (used in metrics labels, Kafka `group_id`, logging).

batch_timeout_ms.description: Max wait (ms) for a full batch before processing a partial batch.

SourceConfig.description:
Source configuration: the bus topics to consume, or the Push listener to
accept records on.

listen.description: Address the Push listener binds on the direct transport.

max_buffer_bytes.description:
Bytes of fetched records librdkafka holds ahead of the pipeline, set
as `queued.max.messages.kbytes`. One fetch can overshoot it by up to
`max.partition.fetch.bytes`.

statistics_interval_ms.description:
librdkafka statistics emission interval (ms). 0 = disabled.
The statistics carry the broker RTT, consumer lag and queue depth
metrics on `/metrics`, and the lag `/scaling/pressure` reports, so 0
leaves the KEDA lag signal at zero.

acknowledgements.description:
On (the default), the source is acknowledged -- a Kafka offset commit, a
Push answered OK -- only once the transformed records are delivered to
the sink, so a crash or a failed send re-delivers rather than loses them.
Off, it is acknowledged at receipt.

Transport.description:
Which transport a stage uses.

One deployment runs one of them: `bus` is a broker between the stages, `direct` is gRPC between them and needs no broker at all. The record and the transform are identical either way -- only who hands the record over changes. `kafka` and `grpc` are read as the same two, the names dfe-engine renders, and a config always writes `bus` and `direct` back.

oneOf.description: Kafka topics.
A scalo Push listener (source) or client (sink).

SaslConfig.description:
SASL authentication for Kafka.

`password` is a [`SensitiveString`] so every serialise path redacts it by
type rather than by a reader's field-name heuristic, and the emitted config
schema carries `x-scalo-secret` + `writeOnly` on the field by construction.

mechanism.description:
SASL mechanism: plain, `scram_sha_256`, `scram_sha_512`, or librdkafka's
`PLAIN`, `SCRAM-SHA-256`, `SCRAM-SHA-512`, in any case.

TlsConfig.description:
TLS configuration for Kafka: `enabled` and `skip_verify` beside scalo's
client `tls` section (`profile`, `trust`, `ca_paths`, `client_cert_path`,
`client_key_path`).

profile.description:
`strong` (default), `commercial` or `cnsa2`. Per-profile settings, such
as `allow_tls12`, live in the `tls.profiles` cascade section.

ca_paths.description:
CA PEM files, trusted beside the OS store under `native` and
`platform`, and alone under `bundle`. One path or a list.

client_cert_path.description: Client certificate PEM for mutual TLS, with `client_key_path`.

client_key_path.description:
Client private key PEM for mutual TLS, with `client_cert_path`. May
name the same file when it holds both.

pin_sha256.description:
SHA-256 pins on the server's public key, as in [`SpkiPin`]. Once the
chain verifies, the key must match one. Empty checks no key.

server_name.description:
The name checked against the server's certificate and sent as SNI.
Default the endpoint's host.

key_share.description:
`profile` (default) sends the profile's first group, a post-quantum
one. `classical` sends a classical share first.

CryptoProfile.description: A named TLS profile. `strong` is the default.

oneOf.description:
TLS 1.3 only unless the profile sets `allow_tls12`, AES-256-GCM,
ChaCha20 and AES-128-GCM, hybrid post-quantum key exchange first.

TLS 1.3 and 1.2, every ECDHE AEAD suite, hybrid post-quantum key
exchange first: the cheapest profile that is still current.

TLS 1.3 only, AES-256-GCM, ML-KEM-1024 then P-384, ECDSA P-384 and
ML-DSA-87 signatures. The CNSA 2.0 shape.

TrustChoice.description:
Which certificates a client accepts a server's certificate from.

Every choice trusts the CA files given beside it, and `bundle` trusts
nothing else.

oneOf.description:
The OS root store, read through `rustls-native-certs` and checked by
rustls.

The OS verifier, through `rustls-platform-verifier`, so Windows and
macOS apply their own policy and revocation checks.
Only the CA files given: an exclusive pin, with no OS root trusted.

SpkiPin.description: SHA-256 of a server certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, in base64 or 64 hex digits.

KeyShare.description: Which key share a client sends first.

oneOf.description: The profile's order: a post-quantum group first where it has one.

A classical group first, with the post-quantum groups listed but not
shared, for a receiver behind a middlebox that drops the larger
ClientHello. A server that prefers a post-quantum group asks for it in
a second round trip.

AcknowledgementsConfig.description:
The `acknowledgements` section of an ack-capable transport.

With `enabled: true` (the default) a source releases its acknowledgement --
a Kafka offset commit, a gRPC or HTTP response -- only once every piece of
work built from the record has been delivered, dead-lettered with the DLQ's
confirmation, or dropped by policy. A failed delivery withholds it, so the
record is delivered again: duplicates are possible, loss is not.

With `enabled: false` the source acknowledges at receipt, before the record
is processed: a crash or a failed delivery loses what was acknowledged.

```yaml
kafka:
  acknowledgements:
    enabled: true
```

enabled.description: Hold the source acknowledgement until every piece is delivered.

SinkConfig.description:
Sink configuration: the bus topic to produce to, or the Push listener to
send the transformed records on to.

endpoint.description: Downstream Push listener on the direct transport, e.g. the loader.

key_field.description: Event field path for Kafka partition key (e.g., ".`org_id`").

compression.description: Compression: none, gzip, lz4, snappy, zstd.

max_buffer_bytes.description: Maximum producer buffer size in bytes.

dir.description: Directory to load all .vrl transform files from (sorted by filename).

files.description: Explicit list of .vrl file paths (loaded in order).

EnrichmentTableConfig.description:
Enrichment table configuration.

Supports two config formats:
- **New (tagged):** `source` field with type-tagged enum (`file`, `mmdb`, `stix`, `sqlite`)
- **Legacy (flat):** `path` + `key_columns` only (treated as `File` with auto format detection)

path.description: Path to enrichment data file (legacy flat format — kept for backwards compat).

key_columns.description: Lookup key column(s). Multiple columns are concatenated with `\x00`.

source.description: Source definition (new tagged format). Takes precedence over `path`.

schema.description:
Per-column type coercion, matching Vector's file enrichment table
`schema`. Without an entry a CSV cell stays a string, so
`status_code: integer` is what makes `{"status_code": 1}` match, and a
`timestamp` column is what makes a `{"from": ..., "to": ...}` date
range able to match at all. Accepted values: `asis`, `bytes`,
`string`, `int`, `integer`, `float`, `bool`, `boolean`, `date`,
`date|<format>`, `timestamp`, `timestamp|<format>`. `asis` and
`bytes` leave the cell alone.

max_bytes.description:
Maximum materialised table size in bytes. A load over it fails startup,
and a refresh over it is refused and the table keeps the rows it has.

EnrichmentSourceConfig.description:
Source definition for an enrichment table. A key the source type does not
have fails the load.

oneOf.description: A STIX 2.1 bundle on disk.

FileFormat.description: File format for enrichment table loading.

interval_secs.description: Refresh interval in seconds. Minimum enforced: 60.

queue_capacity.description:
Bounded mpsc capacity. When the queue is full, `try_send` returns
`QueueFull` (overflow=Drop). Sized for failure-burst tolerance.
Default 10_000.

batch_size.description:
Drain coalesces up to this many entries into one backend write.
Default 256.

flush_interval_ms.description:
Flush a partial batch after this duration, even if not full.
Default 100 ms.

max_payload_bytes.description:
Bytes an entry's payload and copied header values keep together: a
longer payload is cut and the entry marked `truncated` with its
original length, so it lands where the whole record could not, and a
header value that does not fit is left out. `None` keeps every
payload whole. Default [`DEFAULT_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES`].

DlqMode.description: How backends are used when multiple are enabled.

oneOf.description:
Try backends in order. Stop on first success.
Default order: Kafka first, file fallback.

Write every batch to all enabled backends. The write succeeds when at
least one backend takes the whole batch, and fails only when none does.
File backend only (no Kafka dependency).
Kafka backend only (matches a typical consumer's current behaviour).

FileDlqConfig.description:
File-based DLQ configuration.

Writes NDJSON files with automatic rotation and cleanup.

path.description:
Base directory for DLQ files.
Service name is appended as a subdirectory. Default `/var/spool/scalo/dlq`.

max_age_days.description: Auto-cleanup files older than this many days.

compress_rotated.description:
Codec for rotated files past the six newest: `none`, `gzip` or `zstd`.
Default gzip.

level.description: Level, by codec: gzip 1-9, zstd 1-22. Unset, the codec's default.

max_bytes.description:
Rotate before a write that would take the file past this many bytes.
A write into an empty file always lands, however large. Unset: no size
rotation. Works beside the time rotation: either rotates.

max_files.description:
Rotated files kept, newest first. Older ones are deleted at each
rotation. Unset: no count limit, only the age limit. Under `numbered`,
the highest number kept, and `0` deletes the file at each rotation.

naming.description: How rotated files are named: `stamped` (default) or `numbered`.

durable.description:
Sync the file's data to disk after each write, and its directory after
the file is created or rotated, so a write that returned `Ok` survives
power loss. Costs a disk flush per batch. Off by default.

file_mode.description:
Mode for files the writer creates, before the umask. Unset: `0666`
before the umask, except in the file transport, where it is `0600`.
Unix only: a Windows file takes its folder's ACL. Existing files keep
theirs.

dir_mode.description:
Mode for directories the writer creates, before the umask. Unset:
`0777` before the umask, except in the file transport, where it is
`0700`. Unix only.

RotationPeriod.description: File rotation period, by local time.

oneOf.description: Rotate before the first write in a new hour.
Rotate before the first write on a new day.
No time rotation. `max_bytes` can still rotate the file.
`<file>.<local YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>`, adding `.1`, `.2` within one second.

`<file>.1` newest to `<file>.<max_files>` oldest. Each rotation moves
every number up one. No compression and no age limit: their keys are
refused beside it.

FileMode.description: Unix permission mode in octal, such as "0600". Ignored on Windows.
